purpose: This medication is used to treat sudden attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE), a rare genetic condition that causes episodes of severe swelling in the face, throat, abdomen, hands, feet, or genitals. It works quickly to stop these swelling attacks in adults and teenagers. It is not used as a daily preventive medicine, but rather when an attack is happening.
how_it_works: People with HAE are missing or have low levels of a natural protein in the blood called C1 esterase inhibitor. Without enough of this protein, certain chemical signals in the body go out of control and cause swelling. This medicine replaces that missing protein, helping to calm down those signals and stop the swelling attack.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, nausea, and diarrhea. Some people may experience a rash or itching at or near the injection site. These effects are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to rabbits or rabbit-derived products, because this medicine is made using rabbit cells and could cause a serious allergic reaction. Seek emergency help right away if you experience trouble breathing, chest tightness, dizziness, or a severe rash after receiving this medicine. Also let your doctor know if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or have a history of blood clots.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given as an injection into a vein (IV infusion) by a healthcare provider. The usual dose is based on your body weight, typically 50 units per kilogram. A second dose may be given if symptoms do not improve after one hour. It is only used during an active HAE attack, not taken daily.
